name: Vladimir Litvinenko
name_chinese: 弗拉基米尔·利特维年科
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2019-2026)
forbes_bio: Vladimir Litvinenko owned about 21% of publicly traded Russian chemical company PhosAgro. In May 2022 he transferred that stake to his wife Tatyana Litvinenko.
Since 1994, Litvinenko has been rector of Saint Petersburg Mining University.
He chaired the committee that awarded president Vladimir Putin his Ph.D in 1997.
According to Litvinenko, he was one of the creators of PhosAgro's development strategy; as a reward he became a shareholder of the company.
Other sources say Litvinenko was given his PhosAgro shares for political support and lobbying.
forbes_facts: In the 2000s, Litvinenko served as Vladimir Putin's presidential campaign manager in Saint Petersburg three times.
Litvinenko is the author of more than 150 scientific papers and has 47 patents and inventions.

name: V. Prem Watsa
sec_insider_companies: Under Armour, Inc. (UA) - TenPercentOwner; Kennedy-Wilson Holdings, Inc. (KW) - Director,TenPercentOwner
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2015-2025); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Prem Watsa founded Toronto-based financial services firm Fairfax Financial Holdings in 1985 and remains its chairman and CEO.
Born in Hyderabad, India, Watsa later joined his brother in Canada, and then enrolled in the University of Western Ontario's MBA program.
He paid his way through school by selling appliances door-to-door and, after a stint as an investment analyst, struck out on his own in 1984.
He began acquiring insurance companies, modeling his business after the success of his idol, Warren Buffett.
Fairfax now has property and casualty insurance and reinsurance interests across the world plus stakes in companies that include BlackBerry and GE.

name: Herb Chambers
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2016-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Herb Chambers made his fortune as a major New England auto retailer, with 60 dealerships at the company's peak. He sold all but one of his stores to Asbury Automotive in July 2025.
Chambers grew up in Boston's working-class Dorchester neighborhood, where he got his first job as a cart collector at the local supermarket.
He dropped out of high school during his senior year and joined the U.S. Navy.
After returning, he borrowed $500 from his mother to start his first company, a copy distributor, which he sold for $80 million in 1983.
Chambers then stumbled into the car sales business, purchasing a Cadillac dealership that had given him poor service.
forbes_facts: An avowed car fanatic, Chambers owns vintage Ferraris and a Shelby Cobra.

name: Song Chi-hyung
forbes_bio: Song Chi-hyung is cofounder and chairman of Dunamu, which operates Upbit, South Korea's largest crypto exchange by daily trading volume.
In November 2025, South Korean search engine behemoth Naver said its payment arm, Naver Financial, will acquire Dunamu in a stock swap that values the combined entity at $13.6 billion.
Dunamu's previous investors include Kakao Ventures, Silicon Valley-based venture capital firm Altos Ventures and Hybe, the agency behind K-pop powerhouse BTS.
Before starting Dunamu with Kim Hyoung-nyon, who is also a billionaire, Song worked at local mobile payment company Danal.

name: Timm Oberwelland
forbes_bio: Oberwelland's great-grandfather, August Storck founded the business in the Westphalia town of Werther in 1903.
At the time, sweets typically were sold unpackaged and without branding. He packaged his individually and gave them snappy names.
Today, Storck employs over 7,000 people, sells products in more than 100 countries and generates almost $3 billion in estimated annual revenue.
His brother, Axel, became the fourth generation of his family to lead the company after his father, Klaus, retired on Storck's 100th anniversary in 2003.

name: Or Wai Sheun
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2007-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun China (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: Or Wai Sheun runs Kowloon Development, which boasts a portfolio of projects across Hong Kong, Macau and mainland China.
The company has mainland projects in Shenyang, Wuxi, Tianjin and elsewhere.
In 2021 Or took Polytec Asset private from the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. It was formerly a Kowloon Development subsidiary involved in the oil  and ice-storage businesses.
Kowloon Development also distributes films.
His wife and son sit on the company's board.

name: Essam Al Muhaidib
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Essam Al Muhaidib is the CEO of Al Muhaidib Group, a Dammam, Saudi Arabia-based family-owned conglomerate.
Al Muhaidib Group invests in companies across consumer products, infrastructure, construction, real estate and finance; Essam owns 28% of the company.
The group was founded in 1943 by his father Abdulkadir, who started out as a food trader before expanding into building materials and real estate.
Essam and his brothers Emad and Sulaiman took over after Abdulkadir's death in 1996; they share ownership with 4 other family members.
Al Muhaidib Group owns shares in at least 16 publicly traded companies in Saudi Arabia and Egypt.

name: Sabrina Benetton
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2019-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026)
forbes_bio: Sabrina Benetton is a daughter of Gilberto (d. 2018), one of four siblings who founded clothing retailer Benetton in 1965.
She and her sister Barbara each inherited part of their father's fortune after he died.
Initially Giuliana knitted sweaters, Luciano and Gilberto took care of sales and financials, and Carlo acted as the product manager.
Benetton's colorful sweaters soon won over Italy, and the siblings expanded abroad with their first store in Paris in 1969.
The family later diversified their portfolio and invested in other sectors, including infrastructure and finance.
forbes_facts: Sabrina studied at the exclusive Swiss boarding school Le Rosey.
In March 2021, Sabrina stepped down from the board of Atlantia, the infrastructure company controlled by the Benetton family.

name: Bruce Wilson
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026)
forbes_bio: Bruce Wilson gets his wealth from a stake in Reece Group, Australia's biggest bathroom and plumbing supplies chain.
Reece also provides HVAC-R (heating, ventilation, air conditioning and refrigeration) to commercial and residential customers.
The company, which has more than 800 outlets across Australia, New Zealand and the U.S, celebrated its centennial in 2020.
His brothers, Alan and John, also have stakes in Reece and are billionaires.
The brothers' father, Leslie Wilson, was a plumber who joined the board of H.J. Reece, then a small listed plumbing supplies company in 1958.

name: Alexander Rovt
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2021); Forbes annual (2009-2020); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Fertilizer tycoon Alexander Rovt has been pouring his money into New York City real estate, including several apartment buildings in Brooklyn.
His most notable holding is 14 Wall Street, a 29-story office tower in Manhattan. It has nearly doubled in value since he paid $294 million in 2012.
Hotel X Toronto, a 404-room luxury hotel and Rovt's largest investment outside of the U.S., is scheduled to open in 2018.
His IBE Trade deals in ammonium-based fertilizer, but has lost most of its value amid the conflict in Ukraine.
Rovt grew up poor in Carpathia, a contested former Soviet territory, and attended the prestigious Lvov State University of Trade and Economics.
forbes_facts: He managed a high-end Hungarian resort in the U.S.S.R. before immigrating to New York, where he first ran a deli and then sold jewelry.
He says he has never invested money in a stock or bond, preferring hard assets like housing.
